Although the practice of dumping munitions into the sea ceased in 1970, a significant amount remains hidden in coastal waters, posing a safety hazard to commercial fisherman, dredge operators, and others who trawl and work the ocean floor.

Tropical storms and hurricanes often develop with little warning.  Extensive damage to small craft often results in loss of life. Monroe County has continued adding to a new artificial reef site off Monroe County with a 10-year permit. The Gulfside Ten Mile Reef site is a 0.25 nautical mile by 0.25 nautical mile square, encompassing 53 acres of sand bottom of which less than one acre of artificial reef material footprint will be deployed during the lifetime of the permit. The site is located in the Gulf of America within federal waters and lies outside of the boundaries for the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary. The center of the site is located approximately 16.7 nautical miles at a bearing of 23° north of Key West at an average depth of 45 feet MLLW. All deployed material will retain at least a 25-ft navigational clearance.
